fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Mara Velez is coordinating a shared photo archive for her family in Tacoma. The collection currently includes scans of prints from her late grandparents’ house, pictures taken by Mara and her brother Tomas, and phone photographs shared by their aunt Celia. They want relatives to be able to find familiar events without requiring everyone to use the same phone or cloud account. Mara is doing the initial setup on a small computer in her study, where the external drive is connected. Her cousin Niko has offered to help label older folders, but he will not be responsible for maintaining the system.

The family agreed to start with one local archive and to make a separate copy on a second drive when Mara is at home. They have not decided whether to keep an additional copy away from the house. Mara said, “I want the first version to be boring and easy to explain.” The archive should be understandable to relatives who are not comfortable with technical settings. The setup guide should explain what the current arrangement does without presenting a possible remote copy as if the family has already chosen it.

Mara has been collecting images in a folder called Incoming. Some arrive with dates in their filenames, while others have filenames such as IMG_4082 or a message-app export name. Tomas has older camera folders organized by year, and Celia usually shares a whole event at once. The family wants the original files retained, even when Mara creates smaller copies for a shared viewing folder. Mara has started grouping material by year and event, but she has not finished checking every scan date. A scan’s file date may reflect when it was digitized rather than when the photograph was taken.

Their first trial import was the 2018 Alder Street reunion. It included 146 phone photographs, 23 scans, and a short video of the cousins setting up folding tables. Celia recognized a picture of the porch as being from the morning before the reunion, although it had been sent with the rest of the event pictures. Tomas identified a second copy of the same porch image in his camera folder. Mara kept both originals while marking the duplicate for review; the family has not agreed on a rule for deleting duplicates. The video has no reliable date in its metadata, but the family knows it was made during that reunion weekend.

Mara wrote a short inventory on paper before configuring the drive. It lists the local archive, the external drive’s label, and the folder where the smaller viewing copies will go. The external drive is labeled Family-Blue and currently has space for the scanned albums and the recent phone folders. The viewing folder is called Family Picks. Celia asked that the guide explain that a viewing copy is not a replacement for an original. Mara has not chosen a photo catalog application, and the family has not selected a shared online service. Avoid implying that either choice has been made.

The initial local configuration is:

[local_archive]
retain_days = 24
allow_remote = false
name = "local-copy"

Mara entered those values during a test run and wants the guide to describe them as the current local configuration, not as settings for a future service. The family has not asked for changes to this block. The guide should preserve the stated values and the name exactly, while explaining only what can reasonably be inferred from the labels and the notes. Mara’s priority for the first test is to check that recent imports appear in the expected local location and that the separate drive copy can be found afterward.

1. For the recurring import, Mara plans to copy new files from Incoming into a dated working folder, check the source folder before moving anything, and keep the originals. When a date is uncertain, she wants to record the uncertainty rather than silently assign a precise date. Event names can be added after a relative confirms them. Niko may help compare filenames and identify likely repeats, but Mara will make any decision about changing or removing files. Their first test should use a small batch from an event that the family can recognize together.

The timing of the second-drive copy depends on whether Mara is at home: when she is home, she can connect Family-Blue and make the separate copy; if she is away, the notes do not specify an alternate backup action. She does not want the guide to imply that a copy occurred when the drive was not connected. The family has not set a review schedule or settled how long older imports should remain in Incoming. Keep those as unresolved details rather than filling them in. Mara wants to revisit them after the first two import sessions, once she knows how long checking dates and duplicates takes.

At the end of the trial, Mara will ask Celia and Tomas to look through Family Picks on the study computer and confirm that the reunion pictures are easy to recognize. That review is about finding and viewing files, not approval of a permanent archive policy. Celia’s main concern is that family members can distinguish smaller viewing copies from originals, and Tomas wants the older year folders to remain recognizable.
